report_only.title: CLI_RECOMMENDED_VERSION not mechanically enforced against cli_caps::mins — silent drift risk
report_only.symptom: When a new capability gate is added to cli_caps::mins (Rust) above version 2.1.170, `CLI_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` must be manually bumped in lockstep. Nothing enforces this: no test, no assertion, no CI check. A missed bump means Rift shows users 'all features enabled' for their CLI version when a new spawn flag is actually missing.
report_only.fix: Add a vitest test that imports `CLI_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` and asserts it equals the version string produced by the highest `mins::*` constant (extractable via a tiny Rust build.rs print or a generated TS const). Alternatively, move the recommended-version constant to a shared source (e.g., a generated file from Cargo metadata) so there is a single source of truth.

report_only.title: initInner early-exit guard (`unlistens.length > 0`) can silently no-op a legitimate re-init
report_only.symptom: If `destroy()` fires while `initInner()` is awaiting a `listen()` call, then `init()` is called again before the in-flight `initInner()` reaches its gen-check cleanup (line 1046), the old `initInner()` pushes new unlisten entries to `this.unlistens` (now a fresh empty array after `destroy()` cleared it). The new `initInner()` reads `unlistens.length > 0` (seeing those entries) and returns early as
report_only.fix: Remove the `unlistens.length > 0` guard and rely solely on the gen-check already at line 1046. The `initPromise ??=` guard prevents normal concurrent calls; the gen check handles the destroy-during-init case. Alternatively, `destroy()` should set a `destroying = true` flag that `initInner` checks synchronously after each await instead of relying on array-length.

report_only.symptom: If local_llm_base_url points at an https:// LiteLLM proxy behind a corporate MITM proxy (valid enterprise setup), all four probe commands fail with TLS cert errors while real turns succeed (Node.js uses NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS). If the 180s create-model timeout (assistant_optimize_local_model) needs its own value, add a third singleton `certs::probe_client()` with that timeout, or build one with `certs::build_client(Duration::from_secs(180), None)` stored in a OnceLock

report_only.title: nothink.rs: pooled UPSTREAM client skips corporate cert injection
report_only.symptom: The no-think shim's upstream client (used on every proxied /v1/messages turn in local-LLM mode) is built via reqwest::Client::builder() without loading native certs. If local_llm_base_url is an https:// LiteLLM endpoint behind a corporate MITM proxy, every turn silently fails TLS verification. The shim comment at line 32 notes it fixed per-request client churn but didn't address the cert gap.
report_only.fix: Replace the custom `upstream_client()` builder with `crate::certs::usage_client()` (or a dedicated certs singleton if a different timeout is needed). The pool_idle_timeout(90s) behavior is available via `certs::build_client` if a dedicated singleton is warranted.

report_only.title: Fresh webrtc-vad instance allocated every rolling-window tick (already-known #46 R10)
report_only.symptom: Every 1-second rolling-window inference tick calls `window_has_speech`, which allocates a new `Vad` object via FFI (webrtc-vad C heap) and initializes its state machine from scratch. At 1 Hz this is low-frequency, but the FFI alloc + C-side initialization is non-trivial and can spike the 1 s tick latency by several ms on slower machines. Catalogued as #46 R10.
report_only.fix: Construct one `Vad` per `rolling_window_loop` invocation (outside the tick loop) and reset its state between windows using `Vad::reset_state()` or equivalent, or cache it in `ActiveSession`. Already catalogued — noting per scope instructions.
